title: Annotatio VI §.VI close: Concord = sacrament/exhibition not res/reception — stop before §.VII
pass_a_gloss: Reply: The Reformed, after the mind of the older Fathers of the Church, distinguished between Sacrament and Thing of the Sacrament, likewise Exhibition and Reception, and assigned to the Unworthy true Eating and Reception of the former, not of the latter. For so the Concord’s words hold: As Paul says even the Unworthy eat the SACRAMENT, so also those entering the Concord sense that to the unworthy Body & Blood of Christ are truly exhibited and the unworthy TRULY RECEIVE, when the institution & MANDATE of Christ the Lord (also about examining oneself) are kept. But such receive unto judgment, as Paul says, because they abuse the SACRAMENT when they receive without true repentance and faith. For therefore it was instituted, to testify that Grace and Christ’s benefits are applied to those taking and that they are truly inserted into Christ’s Body and washed by his blood who truly repent and console themselves by faith in Christ. The Helvetians’ declaration confirms the same, also reviewed by Crocius, cited place p. 110, and approved by Luther: ibid. p. 111.
pass_b_english: Reply: after the older Fathers, the Reformed distinguished sacrament vs Thing, exhibition vs reception — and gave the unworthy the former, not the latter.

Concord itself: the unworthy truly receive the SACRAMENT unto judgment when they abuse it without repentance and faith; the institution testifies grace to true penitents. Helvetian declaration (and Luther’s approval) confirms. Stop §.VI before §.VII.
source_text: Respond. Reformatos, ad mentem Patrum Ecclesiæ antiquiorum, inter Sacramentum, & rem Sacramenti, item, Exhibitionem, & Receptionem, distinxisse, & prioris, non posterioris Manducationem veram & Receptionem Indignis addixisse. Ita enim verba Concordiæ habent: Sicut Paulus dicit, etiam Indignos SACRAMENTUM manducare, ita sentiunt etiam Concordiam ineuntes, indignis verè exhiberi Corpus & Sanguinem Christi & indignos VERE ACCIPERE, cùm institutio & MANDATUM (etiam de explorando se ipso) Christi Domini servantur. Sed tales accipiunt ad judicium, sicut Paulus inquit, quia abutuntur SACRAMENTO, cùm sine vera pœnitentia & fide accipiant. Ideo enim institutum est, ut testetur, Gratiam & beneficia Christi sumentibus applicari & verè Corpori Christi inserí & sanguine ejus ablui eos, qui pœnitentiam verè agunt & fide in Christum se consolantur. Confirmat idem declaratio Helvetiorum, etiam Crocio recensita, cit. loc. pag. 110. & Luthero approbata: ibid. p. 111.

lemmas.gloss: Sacrament and Thing of the Sacrament

notes: Sacrament not res for Indigni; before §.VII.
